A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Informed Meta-Learning and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices A.1–A.6. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original sinusoidal-regression, weather-prediction and bird-classification experiments, plus additional robustness studies in Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their numerical and graphical results in Section 4 and Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: The INP encoders, aggregation mechanisms, decoder, knowledge conditioning, masking and ELBO training objective remain unchanged, including the task-specific implementations in Appendices A.1–A.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic regression tasks, USCRN temperature data and CUB-200-2011 classification tasks. Distribution-shift and spurious-correlation scenarios are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: The NP baseline and informed/uninformed INP comparisons retain the same membership within the experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.6. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Splits, context/target sampling, classification settings, model configurations and evaluation metrics are unchanged. For example, both retain the 507/108/110 weather-task split and 100/50/50 bird-category split.

E4.justification: The knowledge-format and uncertainty analyses, distribution-shift experiment, and Appendix A.6 studies of training-task count, knowledge complexity and spurious correlations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report standard errors over 110 weather tasks and 60 classification tasks per setting. Table A.3 retains the same bootstrap standard-error reporting and significance highlighting; no run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, A.2 and A.3 retain identical numerical entries, and the plotted results and qualitative findings match. For example, zero-context weather improvements remain 57.7% and 48.1% for setups A and B.

T1.justification: The formal framework, probabilistic assumptions, ELBO derivation and uncertainty decomposition are unchanged, including equations (1)–(15) and Appendices A.4–A.5.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement retain the same claims about formalising informed meta-learning, introducing INPs, integrating loosely formatted knowledge, and improving data efficiency and robustness.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations concerning underfitting, scalability, training-task availability, knowledge complexity and spurious correlations remain unchanged. The added societal-impact statement is generic and introduces no substantive qualification.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.2 retain the same architectures, hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, encoder-training details and data/model access information. The new funding acknowledgement adds no technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v4 removes the introductory citation and bibliography entry for Zhang et al. (2021), Adaptive Risk Minimization: Learning to Adapt to Domain Shift. The remaining research positioning and Appendix A.3 discussion are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes small introductory wording edits, changes citation and heading styles, updates affiliation/publication text, and adds Section 6 acknowledgements and a generic societal-impact statement. The substantive narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The workshop template changes title/header styling, caption typography, spacing and local text/figure placement. The same figures, panels, axes, legends and table structures are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 adds a funding disclosure and workshop formatting while retaining the same method, empirical evidence, reproducibility details and substantive limitations throughout the appendices. The small editorial changes and removal of one supporting citation do not materially strengthen or weaken the paper.
